apps.descripcion_corta: Aidoku is a free and open-source manga reader for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, offering a customizable reading experience with library management, downloads, tracking, and local file support.
apps.descripcion:
Aidoku is a free and open-source manga reading application designed for Apple's platforms, including iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. It provides a modern and customizable reading experience with tools for browsing, organizing, and managing personal manga libraries.

The application includes customizable reading options, downloads for offline access, local CBZ file support, and integration with tracking services such as AniList and MyAnimeList. Aidoku also offers additional features including OCR dictionary lookup and support for compatible reading services.

As an actively developed open-source project, Aidoku provides a flexible manga reading experience across Apple's ecosystem while focusing on library management, customization, and cross-platform support.

apps.descripcion_corta: AniDash – Open-source anime streaming, tracking, manga and offline download app for Android.
apps.descripcion:
AniDash is a free and open-source anime and manga client built with Flutter. It combines anime discovery, streaming, watch-progress tracking, and manga reading in a customizable cross-platform application.

The application provides anime search and discovery, subtitle and dub source handling, local watch history, filler episode detection, manga reading, and playback customization. It also supports integrations with services such as AniList and MyAnimeList-related metadata, while community extensions can provide additional source functionality.

AniDash is developed using Flutter and Dart, with support for Android and Windows. The project is released under the Apache-2.0 license and provides its source code and releases publicly through GitHub. The developers describe AniDash as a client application, with content availability depending on configured sources and third-party services.

apps.descripcion_corta: AniZen is a free and open-source Android anime and movie client built with Jetpack Compose, offering a customizable media player, library management, tracking, offline playback, and advanced video processing features.
apps.descripcion:
AniZen is a free and open-source Android anime and movie client built with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. Developed as a solo project using foundations from Aniyomi and Anikku, it focuses on providing a modern, responsive interface and an advanced media playback experience.

The application includes a customizable video player with features such as Anime4K-based upscaling, motion interpolation, video filters, adaptive shader scaling, and hardware and software decoding options. It also provides tools for managing an anime library, tracking viewing progress, downloading content for offline playback, and creating backups of library data and settings.

AniZen supports tracking services including AniList and MyAnimeList, along with features such as AniSkip integration, local media support, customizable player controls, and extension management. The project is open source under the Apache-2.0 license and continues to receive regular updates and preview builds.

apps.descripcion_corta: Anikku is a free and open-source anime application for Android, offering a customizable experience for discovering, organizing, tracking, and watching anime.
apps.descripcion:
Anikku is a free and open-source anime application for Android, based on Aniyomi and developed with additional features and customization options. It provides tools for discovering, organizing, and watching anime while allowing users to personalize their experience through themes, color palettes, library categories, and player settings.

The application supports anime tracking services such as AniList, MyAnimeList, Kitsu, and others, helping users keep track of their viewing progress and libraries. Anikku also includes support for local media, downloads, backups, extensions, and various additional features contributed by its development community.

As an actively developed open-source project, Anikku focuses on providing a flexible and customizable anime experience while building upon the wider ecosystem of related open-source Android applications.

apps.descripcion:
Animiru is a free and open-source Android application focused on video playback and library management. Developed as a fork of Aniyomi, it provides users with tools to organize their libraries, track their viewing progress, and watch compatible video content through a customizable media player.

The application includes local playback for downloaded content, a configurable player with various settings, library categories, support for tracking services, light and dark themes, and backup options. These features allow users to personalize their experience and manage their viewing data more easily.

As an open-source project, Animiru builds upon the wider ecosystem of related Android media applications while focusing primarily on providing a flexible video player and library management experience.

apps.descripcion:
Anirumy is a free and open-source Android client for AniList, designed to provide a modern way to discover and manage anime and manga. It connects directly to AniList's services, allowing users to synchronize their lists and keep track of their anime and manga activity.

The application includes tools for browsing trending, seasonal, and popular titles, searching for media, viewing detailed information about characters and staff, and interacting with AniList activities and discussions. It also provides airing schedules, notifications, custom Material You theming, dark and AMOLED modes, and an image gallery with downloadable content.

Anirumy is built natively for Android and is derived from open-source AniList client projects, including AniHyou. It is an independent community project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by AniList. The project is licensed under GPLv3 and makes its source code publicly available.

Its downloading system supports concurrent chapter and content fetching, local processing, and flexible source integration, while keeping source-specific logic separate from the core reading and library experience.

Dartotsu is a Flutter rewrite of Dantotsu: one app to track and manage your anime, manga and novel lists, on Android, iOS, Windows, Linux and macOS.

It tracks with AniList, MyAnimeList, Simkl, Kitsu, MangaBaka and MangaUpdates.

Features

Tracking

 Six services side by side, each with its own home, browse tabs, search, calendar, notifications and settings.
 List editor, progress, scores and dates; offline edits are queued and sent when the connection returns.
 List sync between services (one-way, or whichever entry is ahead), with rate-limit aware batching.
 Profiles, activity feeds, stories, groups and Dantotsu comments on every title.
 Trace.moe image search, episode metadata (filler, recap, thumbnails) and a Resume shelf on Home.

App

 Material 3 theming with dynamic colour, OLED, glass mode and card styles.
 D-pad, keyboard and TV navigation.
 40+ languages, Discord Rich Presence, backup and restore, import from Dantotsu, self-update.

apps.descripcion:
Ichaival is a free and open-source Android client for LANraragi, a web-based manga and doujinshi library manager. It connects to a user's LANraragi server and provides a mobile interface for browsing and reading the archives stored in their library.

The application allows users to search their LANraragi database, browse tags, view archive information, and read supported archives directly from their Android device. It also includes bookmarks for keeping track of reading progress, archive sorting, and a dual-page reading mode for landscape displays.

Ichaival is designed as a companion client rather than a standalone content service, relying on a user's existing LANraragi installation. The project is written in Kotlin, supports Android 5.0 and newer, and is released under the GPLv3 license.

apps.descripcion_corta: Kotatsu was a free and open-source manga reader for Android, offering a customizable reading experience with library management, offline reading, tracking, and synchronization features.
apps.descripcion:
Kotatsu was a free and open-source manga reader for Android designed to provide a flexible and customizable reading experience. The application included tools for discovering and organizing manga, managing favorites, tracking reading history, creating bookmarks, and downloading chapters for offline reading.

Kotatsu featured multiple reading modes, including standard, right-to-left, vertical, and webtoon layouts, along with extensive customization options. It also supported local files, reading progress tracking, notifications for new chapters, synchronization between devices, and integration with several manga tracking services.

The original Kotatsu project was discontinued in November 2025, and its official repository was archived. Despite the end of active development, Kotatsu remains a notable open-source manga reader known for its extensive features, customizable interface, and contribution to the Android manga reader community.

apps.descripcion:
Miyo is a free and open-source manga and comic reader for Android, designed for managing large libraries and providing a customizable reading experience. It is a rebranded continuation of Usagi, which itself was derived from Kotatsu, while adding its own changes, fixes, and performance improvements.

The app supports multiple reading layouts, including paged, continuous, and webtoon-style modes, along with bookmarks, reading history, customizable reader settings, and offline reading. Users can organize their libraries with categories, favorites, reading status, and update checks, while local manga directories and CBZ archives can also be managed within the application.

Miyo also supports source plugins, allowing additional sources to be added separately from the core application. Other features include tracking support, backups and restoration, download management, local content indexing, and optional app protection with password or biometric locking.

As an open-source project, Miyo continues the development lineage of Usagi and Kotatsu while introducing its own interface, performance improvements, download system, and other enhancements for Android users.

apps.descripcion:
Tachiyomi was a popular open-source manga reader for Android, first released in 2014. It provided users with a flexible and highly customizable reading experience, allowing them to organize personal libraries, track reading progress, read offline, and access content through community-developed extensions. With customizable reading modes, categories, and extensive library management features, Tachiyomi became one of the most widely recognized manga reader applications in the Android community.

In January 2024, Tachiyomi's development was discontinued following legal pressure and DMCA-related requests connected to copyright concerns. The project's official repository and online services were subsequently shut down, marking the end of active development. Despite its discontinuation, Tachiyomi's influence continued through its open-source legacy and various community projects inspired by its design and functionality.

apps.descripcion:
A personal manga shelf for Android for reading, tracking, and organizing AniList.
Tankobun helps you maintain your AniList library, reading progress, sources, downloads, and backups in a beautiful app.

What is Tankobun?

Tankobun is an Android reader and tracking client built around a workflow based on AniList.

It is designed as a personal reading shelf: log in with AniList, explore your lists, open a manga entry, choose a user-installed source when available, read in paginated or webtoon mode, and keep your progress organized.

Tankobun is not a content service, a content server, an extension repository, or a manga source.

What does Tankobun do?

- AniList login and library syncing authorized by the user.
- Explore manga lists, manage status, scoring, custom lists, and progress updates.
- Reader interface with paginated and webtoon modes.
- Local reading status, caching, and optional offline storage for user-selected sources where permitted by the source and applicable law.
- Source selection via user-installed extensions.
- XML backup export compatible with MyAnimeList for AniList lists.
- In-app restoration tools for compatible backup files.

Sources, extensions, and content

Tankobun does not host, upload, index, provide, sell, bundle, or distribute manga, chapters, scans, extensions, source APKs, or URLs of extension repositories.

Tankobun does not include a default extension repository. It does not recommend source repositories, source websites, or places to obtain manga content.

Any source extension used with Tankobun must be added and installed by the user. The user is solely responsible for choosing which extensions, repositories, websites, or services to use and ensuring that their use complies with applicable laws, site terms, publisher rights, and creator rights.

Tankobun is only a reading/tracking client. It does not grant permission to access, copy, download, or redistribute any third-party content.

AniList

Tankobun uses the AniList API with user authorization.

Tankobun is not officially affiliated, endorsed, sponsored, or supported by AniList. The names, trademarks, data, and services of AniList belong to AniList and its respective owners.

Extension compatibility

Tankobun can work with user-installed extensions that follow a compatible extension format used by the manga reader community ecosystems.

Compatibility does not imply affiliation, endorsement, or support of those projects, their maintainers, extension authors, source websites, publishers, or content providers.

All extension code, source integrations, service names, trademarks, and third-party content remain the property of their respective owners.

Privacy

Tankobun is designed to run as a client-side Android application.

Depending on how it is used, the application may store local application data such as reading progress, cached files, downloads, backup files, preferences, and authentication data needed to log into AniList.

Tankobun does not operate a server controlled by this project for manga hosting, content indexing, analytics, tracking, advertising, or user profiling.

Third-party services, websites, APIs, and user-installed extensions may have their own privacy policies and terms.

Disclaimer

Tankobun is provided solely for personal and legal use.

The author does not host, provide, endorse, verify, or control third-party manga content, source websites, extension repositories, or user-installed extensions.

Users are responsible for how they set up and use the application.

apps.descripcion:
Houri is a free and open-source manga reader for Android, forked from Komikku and built upon work from TachiyomiSY and Mihon. It provides a highly customizable reading experience with extensive tools for organizing libraries, managing chapters, tracking reading progress, and reading manga locally or from supported sources.

The application adds a number of features on top of its upstream projects, including hierarchical library subcategories, enhanced chapter and scanlator management, additional tracking services, webhooks, improved Discord Rich Presence, rereading support, customizable feeds, and expanded source filtering. It also includes an updated reader, experimental image decoding, an in-app updater, and improvements for e-ink devices.

Houri also includes optional tools for AI-assisted translation and grammar correction, manga filtering and privacy features, custom cover management, and additional database protection features such as integrity checks, rolling backups, corruption handling, and SQLCipher support.

As an open-source project, Houri builds upon the wider Komikku, Mihon, and TachiyomiSY ecosystem while maintaining its own interface, features, and customizations for Android users.

extensiones.descripcion:
Modules by Paul is a community project that provides a collection of modules for compatible applications. These modules are designed to extend functionality and give users access to additional features and services within supported apps.

The project serves as a centralized resource for discovering and managing compatible modules while contributing to the wider ecosystem of community-developed extensions. Individual modules may provide different functionality depending on their purpose and the applications they support.

AIOStreams was created to give users ultimate control over their Stremio experience. Instead of juggling multiple addons with different configurations and limitations, AIOStreams acts as a central hub. It fetches results from all your configured sources, then deduplicates, filters, sorts, and formats them according to your rules before presenting them in a single, clean list.

Whether you're a casual user who wants a simple, unified stream list or a power user who wants to fine-tune every aspect of your results, AIOStreams has you covered.

Aidoku Community Sources is a community-maintained project that provides a collection of sources for the Aidoku manga reader. These sources can be added to compatible versions of Aidoku and are designed to expand the application's available browsing options.

The project brings together community-developed sources in a centralized repository, making them easier to discover, install, and maintain. Contributors can also participate in the project by creating new sources or helping maintain existing ones.

As part of the wider Aidoku ecosystem, Aidoku Community Sources serves as a resource for users looking to extend and customize their browsing experience within the application.

Bunori Extensions is the official extension repository for the Bunori ecosystem. It provides source crawlers that extend Bunori with additional online novel sources and are distributed as lightweight `.bext` packages.

The extensions are written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly, allowing them to run across supported Bunori environments such as Android, desktop applications, and command-line clients. The repository also provides reusable templates, developer tooling, automated testing, and GitHub Actions workflows for building and publishing extension packages.

Extensions are distributed through a repository index that can be added to compatible Bunori applications. The project is released under the GPL-3.0 license and is maintained as part of the wider Bunori open-source ecosystem.
